name: Kora

verifiedBusinessInfo.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed-Fri 7:30am-4pm; Sat-Sun 9am-4pm (Yelp listing, Nov 2026; single source, site tells visitors to check Instagram)
verifiedBusinessInfo.other: Co-founders Kimberly Camara and Kevin Borja; named for Camara's grandmother Corazon; began 2020 in a Woodside apartment after both were laid off from hospitality jobs; commissary kitchens and Alewife Brewery pick-ups; ~10,000-person waitlist; Sunnyside shop opened March 2025 (soft opening sold out in hours); won inaugural Queens' Best Bakery competition (Queens Chamber of Commerce), July 2025. Menu items: Leche Flan ni Lola (heirloom recipe of founder's late grandmother), Ube Fried Brioche, ube custard-filled doughnut, Salted Egg Ube Babka, Apple Fritter, croissants, scallion pancake croissant, ube ice cream sandwich (summer). No prices shown (only launch-era prices found).

designDirection: A pastry-box identity for a Filipino-American doughnut bakery with a cult following: Bricolage Grotesque (condensed, heavy) paired with Instrument Serif italics, on an ube-violet / leche-flan caramel / cream / cocoa palette with a pandan-green accent. The hero is a giant KORA wordmark whose O is a slowly spinning doughnut-ring photo (radial mask), with an at-a-glance fact column and a rotating 'Queens' Best Bakery 2025' sticker; below, a sticky arched photo beside a dashed 'shelf' of four signature bakes, a sticky-headed story timeline on cocoa (2020 apartment kitchen to 2025 award), and a flan-orange visit card plus hours table. The menu page is a three-column bordered pastry-case board. Motion: ring spin, badge spin, soft scroll reveals; all disabled under reduced motion. Primary CTA: see the case / hours and directions.
